thread:
Maya: P1 customer (Jesse) reporting dedicated pool not scaling up quickly during a sudden surge, getting 429s and a bunch of timeouts. repro attached, cc @Eli
OpsBot: Alert: Dedicated cluster 'cust-4721' surge spike at 2026-03-17T14:02:04Z, provision_queue=137, min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20
Eli: Thanks Maya — can you paste the simple repro steps and the model/route they're hitting? also need their min/max and autoscaler logs if possible
Maya: Repro: they hit an internal batched endpoint with this load generator: `wrk -t4 -c200 -d40s http://dedicated.cust-4721.redwood/api/v1/generate`
Maya: Observed: requests queueing ~30s, many 429s, attach attempts show intermittent `403 billing_hold` for some pods, rest show `attach_timeout`
Jesse: Adding logs from our side: `2026-03-17T14:02:12Z ERROR request failed status=429 msg="no available replica"` then `2026-03-17T14:02:17Z WARN attach failed: 403 billing_hold user=acct-xyz`
Suresh: 403 billing_hold would explain attach retries failing. but autoscaler should still spin up until min/max. what's the autoscaler decision log? any 'scale suppressed' reasons?
Maya: autoscaler logs snippet: `scale_evaluate: desired_replicas=12 current=2 reason=attach_queue>threshold`, then `scale_action: suppressed reason="attach_auth_failure"`
Eli: Hmm — autoscaler suppressed because agent couldn't attach due to billing/auth failures, so desired replicas never realized. that matches 429s. we should confirm whether attach auth failures are transient or customer-side billing hold. Jesse can you confirm billing state?
Jesse: Billing shows active, no holds. we see auth calls sometimes return 200 then a burst of 403s for ~20s, then 200 again. no obvious credential rotates on our end.
Suresh: Could be ephemeral IAM token expiry or rate limit on internal billing service. but two paths: 1) unblock autoscaler so it ignores attach auth for scaling decisions (safer to let infra scale), or 2) fix auth flow. short term, we can change autoscaler policy to allow scaling on pending attach attempts. (would increase risk of orphaned pods if attach truly blocked) :thinking:
Eli: Agreed. ops checklist: - capture `kubectl describe` events for dedicated namespace - get autoscaler trace (`/metrics/scale_trace` endpoint) - check registry/imagepull events and node conditions. Also share the exact attach error stack from runtime (`preflight_attach` logs).
Maya: Pasting runtime attach snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T14:02:16.831Z] preflight_attach: attempt=3 error="403 billing_hold: account temporarily blocked" pool=cust-4721
[2026-03-17T14:02:16.832Z] attach_queue_len=42
[2026-03-17T14:02:17.145Z] preflight_attach: attempt=4 error="attach_timeout"
```
OpsBot: K8s events: Node node-gpu-17: ImagePullBackOff (registry rate-limit) at 14:01:58Z; Pod cust-4721-abc: FailedScheduling (0/10 nodes) due to InsufficientGPU at 14:02:05Z
Eli: So multiple failure modes: some pods failing to attach due to billing/auth, some failing scheduling due to node availability and imagepull backoffs. that explains prolonged scaleout. we need both fixes.
Maya: Quick mitigation for customer: 1) bump min_replicas from 2 -> 6 for their pool (gives headroom) 2) enable warm-pool prewarming (if allowed) 3) temporarily relax autoscaler suppression to ignore attach_auth failures for 60s
Suresh: I'll prepare a cautious policy change flag: `allow_scale_despite_attach_errors=true window=60s max_extra=4` so we don't overprovision permanently. Also recommend changing image pull to use our cached internal registry mirror to avoid rate limits.
Jesse: Do we need to redeploy anything on our side? we're happy to increase min_replicas but want to understand billing auth burst first.
Eli: For root cause we need traces from auth service correlating to the 403 window. @Billing infra team: can you check for short-lived rate limits or token issuer flaps around 14:02Z?
Maya: Customer accepted bump to min_replicas, we applied it at 14:10Z. After that queue length dropped, 429s decreased to near zero within ~90s. still seeing occasional attach failures until 14:12Z.
Jesse: Confirming reduced errors after min bump. remaining 403s stopped after ~2m. thanks.
Suresh: Follow-ups: - investigate billing auth issuer for transient 403s - implement an autoscaler flag to allow limited scaling despite attach auth failures - recommend customers to enable warm-pool for production surge patterns - add doc snippet for support playbook `support/dedicated-surge.md` with quick mitigations
Eli: I'll open a tracking ticket for autoscaler behavior and the new flag. Maya, can you paste the case notes and final commands used to apply min_replicas change?
Maya: Commands used: `redwoodctl dedicated update --customer cust-4721 --min-replicas 6` and `redwoodctl policy set --name allow_scale_despite_attach_errors --value true --ttl 60s`
Jesse: Appreciate the quick help team. leaving channel but will reopen if we see reoccurence. :thumbsup:
Eli: Thanks all. logging ticket and assigning to Suresh to follow up on billing auth. closing thread unless Jesse reopens. :white_check_mark:
